today.h: Soft PCE, Hard Ceiling: Stocks Split Into Quarter-End as the 10Y Hits a 24-Year High
today.c1: The last session of Q3 ended split: the Nasdaq rose 0.24% while the S&P slipped 0.25% and the Dow fell 0.86% — and all three closed at their session lows. August PCE came in cooler than expected (3.4% headline, 3.0% core), pulling October hike odds down to ~35-37% from ~71% a week earlier — yet the 10Y still touched nearly 5.31%, its highest since 2002, and oil bounced after Trump denied he would ease sanctions on Iran. Tech was the only sector to hold gains as a last-hour, quarter-end fade finished the tape.
today.c4:
• Yields are still the ceiling: with the 10Y at 24-year highs, stay short duration — soft data alone won't break the range until Friday's payrolls prove the cooling.
  • Own what has orders: HPE's record day and Micron's blowout print show AI-hardware spend is real — chase the cash flows, not the story stocks.
  • Breadth is the tell: only 1 of 11 sectors closed green — the tape needs non-tech participation (and a cooler 10Y) to break out of its range.

chains.t: ① Main Chain: The Repricing That Wasn't Enough — Soft PCE, Yet a 24-Year High in the 10Y
steps: 8:30am ET: August PCE 3.4% y/y / 3.0% core — both below estimates
October hike odds collapse to ~35-37% (from ~51% Tuesday; ~71% a week ago)
Yields dip on the data — then climb all day: 10Y nearly 5.31%, highest since 2002
Nasdaq +0.24% holds; S&P -0.25%, Dow -0.86% — all three close at session lows
Q3 closes: S&P +2.0%, Nasdaq +2.5% (2nd straight quarterly gain), Dow -2.7%
chains.d: Reduced hike odds helped tech but couldn't pull the long end down — fresh 24-year-high yields sold every rally, and quarter-end flows finished the fade. That contradiction explains roughly 60% of today's action.

news.fact: August PCE rose 3.4% y/y (core 3.0%) — below the 3.7%/3.3% expected and matching downwardly revised July — cooler, but still well above the Fed's 2% target; economists said it may not stop one more hike this year.
The 10Y touched nearly 5.31% — its highest level since 2002 — and held above 5.30% late in the afternoon, extending the climb that has pressured equities all month.
CME FedWatch: odds of a quarter-point hike at the late-October meeting fell to ~35% from ~51% a day earlier as the PCE landed; futures jumped and yields briefly dipped.

The shifting bias toward a Fed hold came after New York Fed President John Williams said there was 'no need for urgency' to raise rates in October; combined with Wednesday's cool PCE, October hike odds slid from ~51% Tuesday toward ~35-37%.

Bond yields fell in the minutes after the PCE report before continuing a climb that is increasingly pressuring equities; by the close, October hike odds were ~37% versus ~71% a week earlier, with a December hike still expected.
The S&P turned lower and the Dow touched session lows in the final minutes of trading; stocks finished mixed on the last session of the third quarter.

chains.t: ② The Split: Tech Was the Only Boat That Floated
steps: AI hardware and software bought: HPE to a record, CRM +1.9%, MSFT/AAPL/AMZN up ~1%
The yield climb clips the tape: Alphabet +3% midday fades to +0.9%
Last hour slides: only Tech stays green (1 of 11 sectors); staples and health sold worst
Dow -0.86% to session lows — its 5-month winning streak ends (-4.3% in September)
chains.d: Lower hike odds powered growth while the long end's new highs crushed everything rate-sensitive — a mixed index masking a violent split: one green sector, ten red, and a Dow that broke a five-month streak.

news.fact: Hewlett Packard Enterprise rallied more than 5% to a fresh record (intraday high $67) after raising its networking growth targets and landing a $1.2B order for AMD-powered Helios racks from Vultr; it closed +3.9%, among the S&P 500's biggest gainers.
Software led the gainers as hike odds fell: Datadog +2%+, Salesforce +2%, with Adobe, Atlassian, Autodesk, Intuit, Microsoft, Palantir, ServiceNow and Workday all up more than 1%.
Alphabet ran +3% at midday but closed +0.9% as the tape faded; the Magnificent Seven ETF (MAGS) finished +0.4%, and five of the six top Dow gainers were megacaps — yet the Dow stayed red.
Information Technology was Wednesday's relative winner as 10 of 11 S&P sectors closed red.

chains.t: ③ Stock-Level Landmines: Moderna's Downgrade, Jabil's -10%
steps: Citi cuts Moderna to 'sell' after its 500% run — MRNA -5.4% to $193
Still the S&P's #2 performer of 2026, behind only Sandisk
Jabil -10% and Conagra -4.9% after earnings; Cal-Maine -0.9%
FactSet +3.8% on the other side of earnings
Boeing -0.9%: its $20B Navy jet win couldn't hold the stock up
chains.d: Single names still swing 5-10% on policy and analyst headlines while the index barely budges — this market's dispersion, not its direction, is the story.

news.fact: Citi downgraded Moderna to 'sell', telling clients the stock's outsized 2026 rally (500%+) left it overvalued; shares fell ~5.4% to close near $193 — still the S&P 500's second-best performer this year behind Sandisk.
Post-earnings movers: Jabil ended down 10%, Conagra fell ~5%, Cal-Maine slipped less than 1%, and FactSet gained almost 4%.
Boeing ended ~1% lower, erasing early gains from a 'multi-billion-dollar' ($20B+) Navy F/A-XX fighter contract won after Tuesday's close.
Robinhood shares slid 3.2% as the company rolled out new active-trading products, including 'Robinhood Agents' that can trade on users' behalf.

chains.t: ④ Oil's Bounce: Trump Says No to Sanctions Relief
steps: Monday-Tuesday supply headlines knocked crude off its war premium (WTI -3.9% Tuesday)
Wednesday: Trump denies he would ease sanctions on Iran
WTI climbs back: settled around $90.4-90.6 (+1.1-1.4% by quote)
Brent +0.9% to ~$103.50; the war's 7th month keeps the Strait bid
Energy the least-bad of the red sectors (-0.1%)
chains.d: With a peace deal denied, the supply-risk premium returned — oil's bounce is the one place today's inflation math got worse, not better.

news.fact: WTI settled up ~1.1-1.4% around $90.4-90.6 (quotes vary) and Brent advanced 0.9% to $103.50 as traders digested Trump's denial that he would ease sanctions on Iran.
No peace progress: the war enters its seventh month and Hormuz risk remains the swing factor for crude and inflation.
Tuesday's -3.6~3.9% drop came as Saudi Arabia ramped East-West pipeline exports right before Trump said he 'offered Iran nothing'.

chains.t: ⑤ Late-Cycle Check: Micron's Record Print and Friday's Payrolls Test
steps: PCE cooling + GDP revised up to 2.2% + ADP +90k = soft-landing data
But core PCE still 3.0%: economists say one more hike stays on the table
Micron after the bell: record FQ4 revenue $54.23B; FY26 $133.19B (vs $37.38B)
Micron stock about -1% in after-hours trading despite the beat
Next: Nike earnings (Thu), then September payrolls (Fri) — the range-breaker
chains.d: The data argues both sides: cooling inflation with solid growth is the bull case; a 3% core and a live December hike are the bear case — Friday's jobs report picks the winner.

news.fact: Micron reported record fiscal-Q4 results: revenue $54.23B (vs $41.46B in FQ3), non-GAAP EPS $33.42; FY26 revenue $133.19B versus $37.38B a year earlier, with a record fiscal 2027 guided on AI-driven memory demand.
Micron shares drifted about 1% lower in early after-hours trading despite the beat, as Micron's call with analysts got under way.

The data stack behind the day: GDP revised up to 2.2% from 1.5%; August real consumer spending +0.6% m/m, the fastest pace in over a year; and ADP private payrolls +90k for September (vs ~75k expected, with August revised down to +36k).
Micron's report lands as investors hunt for evidence the memory boom can keep funding the AI build-out; Nike reports Thursday and the September jobs report lands Friday.

mtd.h: September's Round-Trip, Complete: Dow -4.29% Snaps 5-Month Streak; Only Tech Held
mtd.d: S&P 7,686 → 7,651.5 for the month (-0.45%); a +53bp move in the 10Y rewrote pricing mid-month, leaving only tech standing.
mtd.c1: The month round-tripped: from 7,686 on 8/31, the S&P peaked at 7,764.7 on 9/21 and gave it all back, closing September -0.45%. The 9/16 hawkish hike flipped the regime (cuts to hikes), the 10Y ran +53bp to 5.29%, and the Dow's -4.3% ended a five-month winning streak. Tech (+5%) was the only sector in the green; financials, materials and staples each lost 5%+.
mtd.c4:
• September's lesson: with the 10Y +53bp on the month, only earnings-backed tech held — anchor there until rates stabilize.
  • Dow's streak snapped and October hike odds fell to ~37%: if payrolls soften Friday, the rotation back into cyclicals is the Q4 trade to watch.

chains.t: ① The Flip: From Pricing Cuts to Pricing Hikes — the MTD Core
steps: Late August: rate cuts still the priced path
30Y to 5.64% (+39bp); oil-driven inflation feeds hike pricing
Late Sept: October odds peak ~70%, slide to ~37% after PCE
chains.d: One meeting flipped the month: the Warsh Fed's hawkish hike turned duration into the market's tax collector — and everything outside tech paid.

news.fact: Fed hiked +25bp to 3.75-4.00%; Warsh warned on inflation; the Dow fell ~600 points on the day.
10Y +13.9bp to 5.106% — highest since 2007, biggest one-day jump since April 2025; Nasdaq's record streak ended.
Month-end: 10Y 5.29% (+53bp MTD), 30Y 5.64% (+39bp), and October hike odds re-priced to ~37% after the soft PCE.

chains.t: ② The Round-Trip: A Record at 7,764.7, Then the Give-Back
steps: 9/30: closes the month at 7,651.5 — a round-trip, not a crash
chains.d: September handed back the entire AI-record leg: +1% month at the peak became -0.45% — the grind, not a break.

news.fact: S&P hit 7,764.7 and Nasdaq set a record as AMD reached a $1T market cap — the month's high-water mark.
September closes: S&P -0.5%, Nasdaq +1.9%, Dow -4.3% — snapping the Dow's five-month winning streak.

steps: 9/9: WTI tops $100 for the first time this cycle
chains.d: September oil traded headline-to-headline; every deal-hope rally was a sale until the supply story took over this week.

news.fact: 10Y back above 4.8% as oil rose into the CPI wait; on 9/9 WTI topped $100 a barrel.
After Trump rejected Iran's ceasefire proposal, the premium deflated on Saudi supply; WTI closed the month up ~5% anyway.

chains.t: ④ Cross-Section: One Shelter, Many Casualties
steps: Tech +5.0% — the only sector up solidly
Utilities -6.6%: the rate trade's whipping boy
Semis and mega-caps carried the index pretense
chains.d: The index said -0.45%; the average stock said much worse — dispersion was September's signature.

news.fact: Into month-end, the gap was stark: tech/comm sat at the top while financials, materials and staples each fell 5%+ — with utilities at 1-year lows.

qtd.h: Q3 Ends in the Black: S&P +2.03%, Nasdaq +2.47% (2nd Straight Quarterly Gain); Dow -2.70%
qtd.d: 6/30 7,499 → 9/30 7,651.5: July's earnings run survived a hawkish September give-back; the 10Y's +87bp is why the net gain is only ~2%.
qtd.c1: The quarter's three acts: July rode earnings to fresh highs, August stalled at the 7,800 line, and September handed back roughly half of the run on the Warsh hike and the yield surge. Final score: S&P +2.03% and Nasdaq +2.47% — second straight quarterly gains for both — while the Dow finished -2.70%. Energy (+15.8%) and health (+6.2%) carried; utilities (-13%) were the rate trade's casualty.
qtd.c4:
• The quarter kept its gains — barely. Protect the +2% through Friday's payrolls; October's range is set by the 10Y.
  • Energy and health were the quarter's real engines, not mega-cap tech — a barbell worth keeping into Q4.

chains.t: ① Earnings vs Rates: A 4% Peak Becomes a 2% Gain
steps: September gives back roughly half the run
chains.d: The numerator can't outrun the denominator: a strong earnings quarter netted ~2% because the 10Y took 87bp the other way.

news.fact: S&P 7,499.36 +0.79% to close Q2 — the best quarter in six years: S&P +15.2%, Nasdaq +21.4%, Dow's best H1 since 2021.
WSJ: the best quarter in six years will be a hard act to follow.
Q3 closes: S&P +2%, Nasdaq +2.5% — second straight quarterly gains for both; Dow -2.7%.

chains.t: ② The Rate Regime Switches Engines
steps: Katayama: AI-capex demand is lifting long-end yields globally
chains.d: The quarter's spoiler was written in rates: a hike cycle re-opened mid-stream and repriced everything long.

news.fact: Japan's Finance Minister Katayama pointed to global AI-infrastructure capex demand behind high long-end yields; JPM's Michele said the curve is oversold.

chains.t: ③ Oil Above $90 Is the Regime
chains.d: For a full quarter, oil above $90 wasn't a shock — it was the backdrop feeding the Fed's hawkish turn.

news.fact: U.S.-Israel strikes on Iran started the conflict; Iran retaliated and the Strait of Hormuz was weaponized — the supply threat that still sets the oil bid.
WTI ends the quarter at ~$90.4 (+30% QTD); the war's monthly supply swings remain the swing factor.

steps: Tech +2.7% — carried but no longer alone
chains.d: Strip out the index and the quarter's real winners were oil and pharma — the late-rotation signature of a hike-priced world.

news.fact: Quarter cross-section: energy (+15.8%) and health (+6.2%) led; utilities (-13.0%) and consumer discretionary (-7.2%) lagged.

ytd.h: The Bull Holds Into Q4: S&P +11.77% as +113bp of Rates Rewrite the Playbook
ytd.d: S&P +11.77%, Nasdaq +15.57%, Dow +5.91% through three quarters — AI and earnings carried; the 10Y's +113bp and a seventh month of war taxed the rest.
ytd.c1: Three quarters in, the rally has extended 2025's +16% — breaking 50k in February, 52k in June, then weathering September's yield shock. The 10Y's move from 4.16% to 5.29% (+113bp) is the year's biggest variable; gold, after spiking with the war, closed Q3 down ~3.5% for the year.
ytd.c4:
• With an +11.8% cushion, don't chase — but don't fight the trend either; own energy and the AI capex chain.
  • 60/40's playbook stays broken while the 10Y prints 24-year highs — keep duration short into Q4.

chains.d: The base case isn't broken — dips keep getting bought and the year's gains survived a full rate shock.

news.fact: 2025 closed with a third straight up year (S&P +16%, Nasdaq +19%, Dow +13%); the S&P finished at 6,845.5.
Dow H1 +8.9%, its best first half since 2021; S&P Q2 +15.2%, best since 2020.

steps: War's oil above $90 and tariffs keep inflation sticky
Core PCE still 3.0%, above the 2% target
chains.d: The early-year cut hopes are dead; the hike cycle itself is the year's master variable.

news.fact: 10Y 4.16% → 5.29% (+113bp); 30Y 4.84% → 5.64% (+80bp) — the biggest repricing in two decades.
August core PCE 3.0% — cooler than expected, still a full point above target; Warsh's Fed remains on watch.

chains.d: The rally and the rate surge share one root: AI needs capital, and capital has a price again.

news.fact: Nvidia gained 17% in Q3 (about +22.5% YTD after three quarters), capping a quarter of Trump dinners, media hits and conferences — and its $12.9B Hugging Face deal.
2026's capital cycle: AMD's $8.2B World Labs deal and Anthropic's targeted $2T-plus listing headline a year of relentless AI investment.

chains.d: Every deal-hope rally was a sale — the war is a permanent line item now, not an event.

news.fact: The seven-day ceasefire proposal rejection is this year's latest falsified deal signal; mediators keep working.

chains.d: Real assets and 60/40 both need new playbooks when the risk-free rate moves 113bp in nine months.

news.fact: The dollar is +3.2% YTD (101.47) and set for its largest monthly rise versus the euro in 14 months; gold's war spike has fully retraced — down ~3.5% this year.
